subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should the bundled Slack plugin implement Slack RTS search now, and what exact action-token, retention, scope, and read-target privacy contract should govern `assistant.search.context` calls?
rationale: The requested feature crosses ephemeral Slack action tokens, workspace-wide search visibility, user-token versus bot-token behavior, and OpenClaw's existing Slack read authorization boundary; automation should not choose that permanent security contract.

options.title: Add narrow bundled RTS support
options.body: Implement Slack-owned RTS with ephemeral token handling, typed action schema, explicit read/privacy gating, docs, focused tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Defer to external plugin or ClawHub
options.body: Keep bundled Slack unchanged until maintainers want to own the RTS token and workspace-search security boundary.

options.title: Reject workspace search for now
options.body: Continue supporting conversation history/thread reads only and close future Slack workspace-search PRs unless a maintainer sponsors the privacy model.

recommendation.title: Add narrow bundled RTS support
recommendation.body: Implement Slack-owned RTS with ephemeral token handling, typed action schema, explicit read/privacy gating, docs, focused tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently closed the broad Slack action-parity PR and explicitly routed Slack search back to this issue for a narrower decision.
